subject: TundraAI dedicated tier: throttling artifact investigation and recovery timeline
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@tundra.ai>, devops@tundra.ai
Cc: support@tundra.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brief: observed throttling artifact on your dedicated pool (initial alert)

Hi Helen / Tundra devops team,

Quick note to let you know we observed a transient throttling artifact impacting your dedicated GPU tier in us-west-2 between 08:46–09:03 PDT this morning. Symptoms we saw: sustained tail latency spikes for generation requests (~2–3x normal p95) and short-lived drops in available RA nodes as the autoscaler initiated rapid eviction/replace cycles. The impact affected ~12% of calls for ~17 minutes and correlated with a burst of concurrent warmup requests from a single tenant key.

Immediate mitigation performed by Redwood ops:
- Temporarily disabled aggressive load-shedding policy for your tenant (rolled to safe defaults at 08:56).
- Prioritized KV-prefix cache retention for active sessions to avoid repeated cold-starts.
- Opened an internal tracer (INF-7421) and pulled node kernel/scheduler traces. Logs attached: kernel_logs_tundra_20290720.tar.gz and scheduler_trace_INF-7421.txt.

We are continuing the investigation; current hypothesis: an autoscaler race + load-shedding rule interaction that briefly marked healthy nodes as saturated, triggering eviction and creating a warmup storm.

Next steps (by Redwood):
- Correlate kernel traces with the autoscaler decision graph (target: 48 hours).
- Provide a customer-visible timeline and RCA writeup by end-of-week (2029-07-24).
- If you prefer, we can stand up a 30-min bridge to review evidence — tell me windows that work.

We will also propose a tailored throttling and burst-smoothing policy for your dedicated tier to avoid re-triggering the same cascade.

Apologies for the disruption — I know these spikes impact production latency. I’ll keep you updated as we learn more.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Success 
Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: kernel_logs_tundra_20290720.tar.gz (log archive), scheduler_trace_INF-7421.txt
From: Helen Park <helen.park@tundra.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@tundra.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2029 09:45:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Brief: observed throttling artifact on your dedicated pool (initial alert)

Camila — thanks for the heads up. We saw increased p99 latency from our side (alerts fired around 08:50). We had a spike in inference volume from a scheduled batch job that overlapped with API warmup traffic; that job is being throttled now.

Two asks from Tundra:
1) Please share the initial evidence and recommend immediate config changes we should make on our side (if any).
2) We will need an interim credit for the minutes of degraded performance — let’s discuss what that looks like.

We can join a bridge today after 11:30 PDT.

— Helen
VP Engineering, TundraAI
helen.park@tundra.ai
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2029 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Brief: observed throttling artifact on your dedicated pool (internal coordination)

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Tundra’s reply. They want evidence and a credit proposal; bridge after 11:30. Summary of what we have:

- Kernel traces show multiple consecutive svc loop stalls on three nodes, each followed by an autoscaler health check that marked the node as degraded. Eviction policy then reclaimed work and shifted buckets, causing repeated warmups.
- Scheduler trace (INF-7421) suggests a timing window where the policy that trims KV cache for low-util keys executed concurrently with a burst of new session allocations. That trimmed critical prefixes for their hot tenant which then triggered more warmup ops.

Proposed immediate product actions (we can implement today):
- Add a per-tenant short-term KV lock for active sessions (sticky retention for 60s) — reduces cold-start storms.
- Create a temporary override to relax eviction aggressiveness for Tundra’s reserved nodes while we clear the traces.
- Draft a credit offer equivalent to 15 minutes of allocated node time (TBD commercial amount).

Can you confirm feasiblity of the KV-lock patch and the override? Also advise on what logs we should attach for SOC2 evidence (I included kernel + scheduler; do we need full prometheus snapshots?).

Thanks — cami

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@tundra.ai>, devops@tundra.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, support@tundra.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident: evidence packet, mitigation plan, and credit proposal

Hi Helen / Tundra team — following our bridge on Saturday, here’s the follow-up packet and concrete plan. Please find attached: scheduler_trace_INF-7421.txt and the kernel logs tar. I’ve also attached a short commercial note (credit_proposal_tundraai.pdf). Links to artifacts are below.

Executive summary (concise):
- Root cause: a race between the eviction-driven KV-prefix cleanup routine and a sudden high-concurrency warmup from a scheduled batch job. The merge of these two events led the autoscaler to repeatedly mark nodes degraded and evict work, which in turn created more warmups (a positive feedback loop).
- Impact window: 2029-07-20T08:46:12–2029-07-20T09:03:29 PDT. Affected requests ~12% of p95 traffic; residual user-visible latency until autoscaler settled.
- Immediate mitigations applied: temporary eviction aggressiveness override; KV-prefix sticky retention enabled for active sessions; hot-tenant burst smoothing applied at the routing layer.

Planned deliverables and timeline:
- Evidence packet & log links (today): https://drive.redwood.com/s/TUNDRA-Audit-Packet-2029-07-24
- Full RCA writeup (including sequence diagrams and root-cause timeline): delivery by 2029-07-24 EOD.
- Engineering fix: KV-lock sticky retention rollout to your reserved pool (canary 10% by 2029-07-25, full rollout 2029-07-28).
- Preventive work: add a gate in the autoscaler to debounce eviction decisions when warmup rates exceed threshold (target delivery: 2029-08-05).

Commercial gesture: attached is a credit proposal equivalent to 15 minutes of node allocation and a $X consulting credit toward a performance review session. We’ll finalize amounts after legal/commercial signoff.

Action items for Tundra (please confirm):
- Confirm a time window to receive the DocuSign credit agreement (I’ve left the default as week of 7/29).
- Provide any additional logs you want included in the SOC2 evidence packet (e.g., external prometheus snapshots).

If you want to schedule a 30-minute technical review next week, I can loop in the runtime team.

Thanks again for your patience — we’re treating this as a priority.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: scheduler_trace_INF-7421.txt, kernel_logs_tundra_20290720.tar.gz, credit_proposal_tundraai.pdf
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2029 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: closure checklist and postmortem owner assignment

Ben / Marissa — closing loop on Tundra. Summary of next internal steps and owners: 

- Formal postmortem writeup (owner: Marissa) — include timeline, decision graph, mitigations, and proposed autoscaler debounce. Due: 2029-07-24 EOD (we’re already late; publish draft now).
- KV-lock sticky retention canary (owner: Ben) — canary target 10% by 2029-07-25; coordinate with infra.
- Commercial approval for credit amount and DocuSign (owner: Camila) — coordinate with legal and finance; aim to have DocuSign ready 7/29.
- SOC2 evidence packet: ensure logs include prometheus snapshots and audit trail (owner: Marissa).

Ben: confirm you can get the canary scheduled tonight. Marissa: I shared the initial draft folder under the INF-7421 ticket.

Thanks — cami
